newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares close down on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares close down on profit taking.

text.p: Jakarta share prices closed down on Friday after sustained local profit-taking on small stocks, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index fell 2.42 points, or 0.44 percent, to close at 547.61 points after touching a low of 546.56 points. Losers led gainers by 52 to 33, with 61 counters unchanged.
Brokers said the lack of market incentives and the uncertainty in regional bourses encouraged some players to cash-in gains which they made in the morning during the afternoon session.
"After making gains in morning session, some brokers took profits in the second session," said one foreign broker.
Brokers said some foreigners bought selected blue chip in small amounts during late trade.
"The market is likely to continue moving sideways next week as many brokers are awaiting for positive news," Pungky Kuntjaraningrat, a research analyst at PT Pentasena Securities, said.
He added prevailing share prices were undervalued and technically the market should be rebound but the lack of positive news was keeping it flat.
Secondline hotel and restaurant firm Mas Murni Indonesia topped the active list with 11.2 million shares traded, rising 125 rupiah to 800 rupiah.
Brokers said the rise was due to a intense market talk of a possible rights issue.

Plywood firm Surya Dumai Industry made significant gains on talk of higher earnings after rises in the price of plywood in international market. It rose 225 rupiah to 2,250 on a turnover of 2.4 million shares.
Brokers said the limited foreign-buying was directed towards Gudang Garam, Semen Gresik amd Bimantara Citra in last session.
Cigarette maker Gudang Garam traded unchanged at 8,600 rupiah on a volume of 466,000 shares, while cement producer Semen Gresik traded unchanged at 6,525 rupiah on a volume of 242,000 shares.
